material_systems.name: Exterior Acrylic Primer for Wood/FC Soffit

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for (1) bare wood soffit — full field prime and (2) factory-primed fiber cement soffit — field prime over factory transit primer (MANDATORY per James Hardie warranty). Coverage is lower than vertical siding application due to overhead waste factor. Overhead application increases drip losses by ~10%. Must be top-coated within 180 days of installation on fiber cement.

material_systems.notes: Shared system — same product covers both bare wood and factory-primed fiber cement. Factory-primed FC has lower porosity (higher end of coverage range). Bare wood T&G has higher absorption (lower end). Apply surface_texture_modifier for T&G rough-sawn boards.

material_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer for Tannin Knots on Wood Soffit

products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: Spot-applied to visible knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, Douglas fir) BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Not a full-surface system — applied per knot/stain location by brush. Alkyd has superior tannin stain blocking vs acrylic. Shellac-based (BIN) for extreme cases. Overhead application makes drip control important — use thixotropic formulation.

material_systems.notes: Conditional on wood species — required for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir). Pine and spruce typically do not require knot spot-priming unless visible knots are present. Applied by brush to individual knots overhead. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 2.

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Bare Fiber Cement Soffit

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
primer.notes: Required for bare/damaged fiber cement soffit (pH 13.0). Prevents saponification (alkaline burn) of latex binders. SW Loxon Masonry Primer is the reference product. Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable for bare fiber cement. Lower coverage than standard acrylic primer — bare FC is more porous. Overhead application adds waste factor.

material_systems.notes: Bare FC soffit uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD by convention when factory primer is absent/damaged. This system is activated when substrate_material = fiber_cement AND factory primer is compromised. Apply within 90 days of bare exposure. Critical for preventing alkaline burn failure (FM-002 equivalent).

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Vinyl Soffit

products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
primer.notes: Mandatory for vinyl (PVC) soffit panels. Chemical bond to dense non-porous PVC surface. Scuff-sand with 220-grit before application. CAUTION: Bonding primer left exposed beyond 1 week loses flexibility — recoat within 1 week. Only 100% acrylic latex binders are compatible with vinyl (no alkyd, no oil-based topcoats).

material_systems.notes: Vinyl soffit uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD state by convention (no dedicated SS_EXT_BARE_VINYL exists). Non-porous surface provides consistent, higher coverage than wood. Bonding primer is non-negotiable — standard acrylic primer will NOT adhere to vinyl.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Soffit Paint

finish.notes: Standard residential exterior acrylic. Flat to satin sheen only (overhead surfaces show imperfections at higher sheen, and soffit has lower durability demands). QT2 allows single finish coat on primed surfaces. QT3 requires 2 coats. Mildew-resistant formulation recommended for sheltered soffit surface — soffits are prone to mildew due to trapped moisture and limited UV exposure.

material_systems.notes: Standard soffit finish system. Flat is the most common soffit sheen. Satin for higher-visibility soffits on wide overhangs. Overhead application requires thin coats to prevent sag — do not attempt heavy film build.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic Soffit Paint

finish.type: Premium 100% Acrylic Exterior with Enhanced Mildew Resistance
finish.notes: Premium materials with superior color retention, fade resistance, and mildew resistance. Light sand between coats (220-grit) on visible areas. Raking light inspection before second coat. Flat to satin sheen. Premium formulation has higher solids — slightly lower coverage per gallon.

material_systems.notes: Premium soffit finish for QT4. Mildew-resistant formulation is especially important for sheltered soffit surfaces on north-facing and shaded elevations. No semi-gloss or gloss — overhead surfaces do not benefit from high sheen.

material_systems.name: Solar-Reflective Paint for Vinyl Soffit

finish.type: IR-Reflective Acrylic with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs)
products: Benjamin Moore Colors for Vinyl (select palette)
finish.notes: CONDITIONAL: Required when vinyl substrate AND color LRV < 55. IR-reflective pigments allow dark visual colors while reflecting near-infrared radiation. HARD STOP — standard dark paint on vinyl causes thermal distortion at ~165 degrees F heat deflection (FM-005). Only 100% acrylic latex binders. Color palette more limited than standard lines.

material_systems.notes: Activated by vinyl substrate + dark color (LRV < 55). When LRV >= 55, standard finish systems are acceptable on vinyl. Slightly lower coverage than standard acrylic due to specialty CICP pigment formulation. Overhead waste factor applies.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Bare wood T&G or plywood soffit. Moderate-to-high absorption on bare wood. Overhead application waste increases consumption ~10% vs vertical. T&G boards at low end of range (groove joints increase surface area).

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: Factory-primed fiber cement soffit — sealed surface, lower absorption. Higher coverage than bare wood. Still includes overhead waste factor.

coverage_profiles.overhead_waste_notes: 10% additional material waste for overhead application (dripping, gravity-fed runs, application angle inefficiency). Already factored into sf_per_gallon rates above.
assumptions: Coverage rates include overhead waste factor — do not apply overhead_waste_factor again at runtime.
Surface_texture_modifier is applied on top of base coverage rate for rough-sawn T&G boards.
Spray application (non-vented only): multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency loss.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Bare/damaged fiber cement soffit (using SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD by convention). Highly porous bare substrate absorbs primer heavily. Overhead application waste adds to consumption. Lowest coverage primer in this spec.

assumptions: Bare fiber cement exposure on soffit is relatively uncommon in NC — typically panels arrive with factory primer intact.
This system is activated when factory primer is damaged or absent. Coverage may drop further if substrate is severely weathered.

SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard acrylic on primed soffit surface. Primed surfaces have consistent absorption. Overhead waste factor included.

SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium acrylic has higher solids content — slightly lower coverage per gallon. Overhead waste factor included.

SYS_EXT_SFIT_FINISH_SOLAR.notes: Solar-reflective formulation with CICP pigments — reduced coverage compared to standard acrylic. Overhead waste factor included.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET soffit area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SOFFIT_FIELD).
Two-coat system is standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single coat on primed surfaces.
Spray application (non-vented only): multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency loss.
T&G boards: apply surface_texture_modifier 1.15 for rough-sawn texture. Smooth T&G panels use 1.00.

consumables.name: 80-120 Grit Sandpaper for Wood Soffit Prep
consumables.notes: 80-120 grit for wood soffit adhesion profile. Overhead use increases consumption — sanding overhead causes faster paper loading and more frequent replacement than vertical work. Hand blocks for T&G grooves, orbital sander for flat panels.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit
consumables.notes: Scuff-sand vinyl soffit (220-grit) before bonding primer. Also used for intercoat sanding at QT4 between finish coats. Overhead use increases consumption. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 Grit
consumables.notes: General prep sanding on fiber cement soffit and intercoat scuff at QT4. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Required after all sanding operations. Overhead work causes more dust to fall away from surface — tack cloth pass ensures clean substrate. Reduced coverage per cloth vs vertical (100 SF overhead vs 150 SF vertical). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Fiber Cement End-Cut Edge Sealer
consumables.notes: Seal field-cut edges on HardieSoffit panels to prevent capillary moisture absorption via cellulose fibers (FM-006). Apply to ALL field-cut edges before or immediately after installation. May share product with CON_FCSD_END_SEALER from siding spec.

consumables.name: Exterior Flexible Paintable Caulk for Soffit Joints
consumables.notes: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic for soffit panel joints and soffit-to-fascia/frieze junctions. Overhead caulking is slower and consumes more per LF due to gravity and application angle. Never use silicone — not paintable. Caulk AFTER primer coat. Allow full cure per sealant type before painting (polyurethane: 3-7 days; siliconized acrylic: skin time only).

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2.5 inch
consumables.notes: Primary brush for soffit detail — cut-in at fascia and frieze junctions, T&G groove work, knot spot-priming, edge detail. Overhead brush work is demanding on brush quality — use premium bristle. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: 1 brush per material type. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Flat Brush 3 inch
consumables.notes: Secondary brush for wider T&G board grooves and panel joint detail. 3-inch flat is more efficient than angular sash for working paint into T&G groove channels on wide boards.

consumables.name: 9-inch Roller Cover for Overhead Soffit
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 300 SF rolled (primer or finish per coat)
consumables.notes: 3/8-inch nap for smooth soffit panels (plywood, fiber cement, vinyl). 1/2-inch nap for T&G boards (textured). Overhead rolling increases drip losses — use low-splash covers. Higher consumption rate overhead (300 SF vs 500 SF vertical) due to paint loading and drip losses.

consumables.name: Extension Pole for Overhead Roller Application
consumables.notes: 4-8 ft extension pole attached to roller frame for overhead application from ladder or scaffold. Allows painter to reach soffit without full overhead arm extension. Reduces fatigue and improves coverage consistency. Reusable across projects.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 413 (non-vented soffit)
consumables.notes: 413-515 tip for soffit spray application on non-vented solid panels ONLY. Spray is PROHIBITED on vented soffit. Tight to medium fan pattern for controlled overhead application. Overhead spraying increases overspray — use lower pressure settings.

consumables.name: 60-Mesh Spray Filter (black) for Latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black) filter for latex exterior coatings through airless equipment. Only applicable when application_method = spray (non-vented soffit).

consumables.name: Plastic Sheeting for Ground Protection Below Soffit
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum for landscape and hardscape protection directly below soffit work zone. UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects. CRITICAL for overhead work — gravity pulls all drips and roller spatter straight down. Brush/roll: drop cloth at base. Spray: full tarp coverage below entire work zone.

consumables.name: Canvas Drop Cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway protection below soffit work area. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Used for fascia edge masking (when fascia is finished), light fixture protection, and general edge masking at soffit junctions. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: all tape rolls yield 180 LF (60 yards). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking Film/Paper for Adjacent Fascia/Frieze
consumables.notes: Masking film or paper for protecting finished fascia and frieze boards from soffit roller spatter. Only needed when adjacent trim is already finished. Tape + 12-inch film along fascia-soffit junction. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Caulk Gun
consumables.notes: Standard caulk gun for tube application. Overhead caulking requires good trigger control. Reusable across projects.

ext_landscape_adjacent.description: Landscape area directly below soffit work zone — drip fallout zone
ext_landscape_adjacent.notes: Ground protection below soffit is MORE critical than siding protection because overhead painting sends all drips straight down. Brush/roll: drop cloth at base captures drips. Spray: full tarp coverage over entire landscape zone below work area (heavy overhead overspray fallout).

ext_hardscape_walk.description: Adjacent walkways and hardscape directly below soffit work area
ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic on walkways. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray. Overhead drip fallout is heavy — canvas must be in place before any overhead work begins.

ext_light_fixture.description: Soffit-mounted light fixtures (recessed lights, porch fixtures)
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over soffit-mounted fixtures. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible. Recessed lights in soffit are common — mask ring and trim with tape.

ext_fascia_adjacent.description: Fascia board above soffit — protect when already finished
ext_fascia_adjacent.notes: Light masking at fascia-soffit junction when fascia is already painted. Tape + 12-inch film prevents roller spatter on finished fascia during overhead soffit rolling. If fascia is unfinished (typical in top-down NC sequence), no protection needed. No dedicated PaintScope key — masking quantity derived from soffit perimeter LF.

ext_siding_adjacent.description: Siding field below soffit at wall junction — protect when finished
ext_siding_adjacent.notes: Light masking at soffit-to-wall junction (frieze area) when siding is already painted. In top-down NC sequence, siding is typically unpainted when soffit is done — no protection needed. If sequence is reversed, mask frieze-siding junction to prevent roller drip on finished siding.

compatibility_rules.description: Acrylic primer for bare wood and factory-primed fiber cement soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer covers both bare wood and factory-primed FC. Field prime on FC is MANDATORY per Hardie warranty — not optional even if factory prime looks intact.

compatibility_rules.description: Alkali-resistant primer required for bare fiber cement soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: Bare fiber cement (pH 13.0) causes saponification with standard acrylic primer. Alkali-resistant primer is non-negotiable when factory primer is absent or severely damaged.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer mandatory for vinyl soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard acrylic and alkali-resistant primers do NOT adhere to non-porous vinyl. Bonding primer creates chemical bond to PVC surface. Non-negotiable.

compatibility_rules.description: Solar-reflective finish required for vinyl soffit with dark colors
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD STOP — standard dark paint on vinyl causes thermal distortion (warping, buckling) at ~165 degrees F heat deflection. Solar-reflective (VinylSafe) coating is non-negotiable when vinyl + LRV < 55. FM-005.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer needed when substrate is field-primed
compatibility_rules.notes: Skip prime module entirely when soffit has already been field-primed. Direct topcoat application.

compatibility_rules.description: Spray application PROHIBITED on vented soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD RULE — spray on vented soffit drives atomized paint into attic through vent perforations. Contaminates insulation, clogs vent screens, reduces attic ventilation capacity. Brush/roll only on vented soffits. FM-001.

compatibility_rules.description: Only 100% acrylic latex binders on vinyl soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: No alkyd, oil-based, or hybrid binders on vinyl substrate. Only 100% acrylic latex is compatible with PVC thermal expansion behavior. Alkyd/oil binders become brittle on vinyl.

compatibility_rules.description: Flat and satin sheen only for soffit
compatibility_rules.notes: Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine section 3: soffits use flat or satin. No semi-gloss or gloss — overhead surfaces show imperfections at higher sheen, and lower sheen is the accepted standard for soffit.

compatibility_rules.description: Caulk AFTER primer coat — never before
compatibility_rules.notes: Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces. Sequence: prep -> prime -> caulk -> finish. Per Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine.

High-pressure power washing is PROHIBITED on soffit. Damages thin panel edges, forces water into attic through vent openings, strips factory primer on fiber cement. Low-pressure wash only (garden hose + soft brush, 800-1200 PSI max).

risk_notes.topic: Attic vent contamination from spray application
risk_notes.risk: Spray application on vented soffit drives atomized paint into attic cavity through perforated panels or vent openings. Contaminates insulation, clogs vent screens, reduces ventilation capacity. Clean-up liability exceeds soffit painting cost.
risk_notes.mitigation: HARD RULE: Brush/roll only on vented soffits. Spray only on non-vented solid panel soffits. When spraying non-vented sections, mask all adjacent vent openings.

risk_notes.topic: Thermal distortion on vinyl soffit from dark paint
risk_notes.risk: Standard dark paint (LRV < 55) on vinyl soffit absorbs excessive heat, causing PVC panels to warp, buckle, or permanently deform at ~165 degrees F.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use solar-reflective (VinylSafe) coating on ALL vinyl soffit with color LRV < 55. HARD STOP — no exceptions.

risk_notes.topic: Edge wicking on fiber cement soffit panels
risk_notes.risk: Unsealed field-cut edges on HardieSoffit panels absorb moisture via cellulose capillaries. Edge swelling ruptures paint film. Overhead position means condensation can pool at panel edges.
risk_notes.mitigation: Seal ALL field-cut edges with end-cut sealer (CON_SFIT_END_SEALER) before or immediately after installation.

risk_notes.topic: Tannin bleed through on cedar/redwood T&G soffit
risk_notes.risk: Cedar and redwood T&G soffit boards bleed tannins through water-based primers and topcoats. Brown/reddish-brown staining appears at knots and board junctions. Most visible with flat white finish — the most common soffit color.
risk_notes.mitigation: Spot-prime visible knots with alkyd or shellac stain blocker (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_TANNIN_SPOT) before full acrylic primer coat.

risk_notes.topic: Mildew growth on sheltered soffit surface
risk_notes.risk: Soffits are sheltered from UV and rain but exposed to moisture condensation from attic temperature differentials. Ideal conditions for mildew, especially north-facing and shaded elevations.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use paint with mildewcide additive or mildew-resistant formulation. Clean soffit with mildewcide solution before painting. Ensure proper attic ventilation.

risk_notes.risk: Overhead application makes paint drips and sags highly visible and difficult to control. Excess material runs to fascia junction or drips onto surfaces below.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply thin coats overhead. Back-brush immediately after rolling. Use extension pole for consistent pressure. Protect all surfaces below before beginning overhead work.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure on vinyl from skipping prep
risk_notes.risk: Painting over glossy vinyl without scuff-sanding causes coating to peel in sheets. Bonding primer alone is insufficient without surface preparation.
risk_notes.mitigation: Scuff-sand vinyl with 220-grit. Clean with denatured alcohol or TSP. Then apply bonding primer.

risk_notes.risk: Bonding primer left exposed beyond 1 week dries brittle — loses flexibility needed for topcoat adhesion bond on vinyl.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply topcoat within 1 week of bonding primer application. If exceeded, scuff-sand before topcoat.

risk_notes.topic: Factory primer degradation on fiber cement
risk_notes.risk: Factory primer on HardieSoffit degrades if exposed beyond 180 days. Becomes chalky, loses adhesion.
risk_notes.mitigation: Field-prime and paint within 180 days of installation. If exceeded, assess adhesion with tape pull test and re-prime if needed.

material_quantity_notes.overhead_waste_factor: All soffit coverage rates already include ~10% overhead waste factor (gravity-fed dripping, application angle inefficiency). Do NOT apply additional overhead waste at runtime.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: T&G rough-sawn boards: multiply material quantity by 1.15x for texture absorption. Smooth panels (plywood, FC, vinyl): 1.00x.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on non-vented soffit: 50-70% transfer efficiency. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25-1.50. Overhead spraying has worse transfer efficiency than vertical — lean toward 1.40-1.50.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: Standard coat system: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats at QT3/QT4 on bare or factory-primed substrate. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime coat. QT2 may use single finish coat.
material_quantity_notes.tg_joint_material_note: T&G board grooves increase effective surface area but are already captured in the surface_texture_modifier. Do not double-count groove area with separate SF measurement.

assumptions.value: 250-350 SF/gal on smooth soffit panels (vs 300-400 SF/gal on vertical siding)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 4, adjusted for overhead waste
assumptions.note: Doctrine provides vertical coverage rates. Overhead adjustment (~10% waste increase) is applied based on research RF-003 and sibling spec pattern.

assumptions.source: Sibling spec COV_FCSD_FINISH (300-400 SF/gal vertical), adjusted for overhead waste
assumptions.note: Finish coverage follows same overhead adjustment pattern as primer.

assumptions.value: Vinyl soffit uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD state by convention
assumptions.source: No dedicated SS_EXT_BARE_VINYL exists in Substrate_State_Reference.md
assumptions.note: May need a dedicated vinyl state in the future. For now, SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is the closest match (bare substrate requiring bonding primer).

assumptions.value: 50 LF per tube (vs 72 LF/tube for vertical NC trim)
assumptions.source: Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md section Caulk, adjusted for overhead waste
assumptions.note: Overhead caulking wastes more per tube — gravity pulls caulk down from the bead, requiring reapplication. No doctrine-specific soffit caulk rate. Estimated at ~70% of vertical trim rate.

assumptions.value: 250-325 SF/gal for IR-reflective paint on soffit
assumptions.source: Sibling trim spec COV_XTRM_FINISH solar-reflective (300-350 SF/gal vertical), adjusted for overhead
assumptions.note: No doctrine coverage for solar-reflective paint on overhead surfaces. Derived from trim spec data with overhead adjustment.

uncertainty_flags.description: The 10% overhead material waste factor is estimated from general industry practice — no doctrine provides a specific overhead waste multiplier for painting materials.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration. Track actual material consumption on soffit vs siding on same project.

uncertainty_flags.description: The 1.15x material modifier for T&G rough-sawn boards is derived from research — no direct doctrine calibration for overhead T&G material consumption.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate against field practice. T&G board width (3.5 vs 5.5 inch) may affect actual consumption.

uncertainty_flags.description: Overhead spray transfer efficiency may be worse than vertical (1.40-1.50x vs 1.25-1.33x for vertical siding). No specific doctrine or calibration data for overhead spray waste.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration when spray on non-vented soffit is actually performed. Limited data — uncommon scenario.

uncertainty_flags.description: Roller cover consumption rate (1 per 300 SF) is estimated — overhead rolling causes faster cover wear from drip loading and continuous overhead pressure.
